fields.What it is: A robot description file lists the links (with masses, inertias and meshes) and joints (type, axis, limits) of a robot. URDF is the ROS standard and MJCF is MuJoCo's format. Simulators, IK solvers and dynamics libraries all read these files, so a wrong file breaks everything downstream.
fields.Prerequisites: Coordinate frames; XML; basic CAD helps
fields.Frontier state 2026: Curated model libraries (MuJoCo Menagerie) ship ready-made arms, quadrupeds and humanoids; CAD-to-robot exporters (onshape-to-robot) produce URDF/SDF/MJCF directly from Onshape assemblies, including kinematic loops.
fields.Key players: Google DeepMind (MuJoCo, Menagerie), Rhoban/Bordeaux (onshape-to-robot), ROS community

fields.What it is: Forward kinematics computes where the robot's hand (end-effector) is, given all joint angles. It chains one transform per joint. The two classic recipes are Denavit-Hartenberg parameters and the product-of-exponentials formula.
fields.Prerequisites: Rigid-body motion & coordinate frames
fields.Frontier state 2026: Solved for serial arms; still the first building block for every controller, IK solver and learned policy that outputs end-effector poses.
fields.Key players: Modern Robotics authors; Springer Handbook ch. 2 (Waldron & Schmiedeler); Stanford CS223A

fields.What it is: The Jacobian is a matrix that maps joint speeds to the hand's linear and angular speed, and joint torques to hand forces. At a singularity the Jacobian loses rank: the arm cannot move in some direction no matter how fast the joints spin. Manipulability measures how close the arm is to that.
fields.Prerequisites: Forward kinematics; derivatives; matrix rank
fields.Frontier state 2026: Standard theory; current tools compute Jacobians, Hessians and manipulability automatically, and differential-IK libraries use them in real time.
fields.Key players: Stanford CS223A (Khatib), Modern Robotics, QUT Robotics Toolbox

fields.What it is: Inverse kinematics (IK) answers the reverse question: which joint angles put the hand at a target pose? Simple arms have closed-form formulas; general arms need iterative numerical solvers that respect joint limits. There can be zero, one or many solutions.
fields.Prerequisites: Forward kinematics; Jacobians; basic optimization
fields.Frontier state 2026: Numerical IK is commodity (TRAC-IK combines Newton and SQP solvers to handle joint limits). The open part is speed and robustness for many-DoF robots and many simultaneous goals.
fields.Key players: TRACLabs (TRAC-IK), MoveIt community, Modern Robotics

fields.What it is: Instead of solving IK once, differential IK computes at every control step a small joint velocity that moves the robot toward several goals at once (hand pose, posture, center of mass) while respecting limits. It is written as a small quadratic program. Robots with more joints than needed (redundant) use the extra freedom for secondary goals.
fields.Prerequisites: Jacobians; least squares; quadratic programs (conceptually)
fields.Frontier state 2026: Task-based QP IK is now the default for teleoperation, humanoid retargeting and whole-body motion. mink handles floating bases and collision limits; Pink does the same on Pinocchio models.
fields.Key players: Kevin Zakka (mink), Stéphane Caron (Pink), Inria/LAAS (Pinocchio)

fields.What it is: Wheeled robots cannot slide sideways, which is a 'nonholonomic' constraint. Differential-drive, unicycle and car-like robots share one simple model that turns wheel speeds into forward speed and turning rate. Integrating this model from wheel encoders gives odometry.
fields.Prerequisites: Coordinate frames; basic calculus
fields.Frontier state 2026: Mature; used everywhere in AMRs and mobile manipulators. Remaining difficulty is wheel slip, which kinematics alone does not model.
fields.Key players: Modern Robotics ch. 13, Caltech, ROS navigation community

fields.What it is: In a parallel robot (e.g. a delta robot), several legs connect the base to the moving platform, forming closed loops. For these, inverse kinematics is often easy and forward kinematics is hard, the reverse of serial arms. Closed loops also appear inside legs and grippers (linkages).
fields.Prerequisites: Forward & inverse kinematics; constraints
fields.Frontier state 2026: Closed-loop support is now native in dynamics libraries (Pinocchio) and CAD exporters (onshape-to-robot closing constraints). Accurate simulation of many coupled loops with contacts is still an active topic.
fields.Key players: Pinocchio team (Inria), simulation researchers; open-source delta builders

fields.What it is: Dynamics links motion to forces: the mass matrix M(q), Coriolis/centrifugal terms and gravity give tau = M(q)q'' + C(q,q')q' + g(q). Inverse dynamics computes the torques needed for a desired motion; forward dynamics computes the motion produced by given torques. This is what physics simulators integrate every step.
fields.Prerequisites: Kinematics; Newton's laws; ODEs
fields.Frontier state 2026: Classical theory (Lagrange, Newton-Euler, Featherstone's spatial algebra). Taught in MIT Underactuated and Stanford CS223A; underlies all model-based control and simulation.
fields.Key players: Roy Featherstone, David Orin (Springer Handbook ch. 3), MIT (Tedrake), Stanford (Khatib)

fields.What it is: Recursive algorithms (RNEA for inverse dynamics, ABA for forward dynamics) compute dynamics in time linear in the number of joints. Modern libraries also compute their exact derivatives, which gradient-based optimizers and MPC need.
fields.Prerequisites: Rigid-body dynamics; C++/Python
fields.Frontier state 2026: Pinocchio (Inria Paris, BSD) provides analytical derivatives of RNEA/ABA, centroidal dynamics, closed loops and frictional contact solvers; it powers Crocoddyl and many humanoid MPC stacks.
fields.Key players: Inria Willow / LAAS-CNRS (Carpentier, Mansard), Featherstone

fields.What it is: A path says where to go; a trajectory also says when. Time scaling assigns speeds along a path so velocity, acceleration and jerk limits are respected. Jerk-limited (S-curve) profiles make motion smooth and protect hardware.
fields.Prerequisites: Kinematics; basic calculus
fields.Frontier state 2026: Real-time jerk-limited generators (Ruckig, <1 ms) and time-optimal path parameterization (TOPP-RA) are mature and used in MoveIt. Active work: combining with collision-aware planners and learned policies' outputs.
fields.Key players: Ruckig (Berscheid/Kröger), TOPP-RA (Pham & Pham), MoveIt

fields.What it is: Identification estimates the real masses, inertias and friction of a robot from recorded motion and torque/current data, because CAD values are wrong. For cheap servos, the friction and motor model often matter more than link inertias. Good identified models shrink the sim-to-real gap.
fields.Prerequisites: Rigid-body dynamics; least squares; logging data from motors
fields.Frontier state 2026: Physically consistent identification (SDP constraints) is standard in research (BIRDy benchmark). Rhoban's BAM (2024-26) fits extended friction models for common servos (Dynamixel, eRob and the SO-101's Feetech STS3215) and plugs into MuJoCo/mjlab for RL sim-to-real.
fields.Key players: Rhoban (Bordeaux), BIRDy authors, Pinocchio regressors

fields.What it is: Real robots differ from their URDF by small errors in link lengths and joint offsets. Kinematic calibration measures the robot in many poses and corrects these parameters; hand-eye calibration finds where the camera is relative to the robot. Both are needed before a camera-guided arm can hit a target.
fields.Prerequisites: Forward kinematics; least squares; camera basics
fields.Frontier state 2026: Recent work removes markers and external sensors, calibrating arm and RGB-D camera together from learned image correspondences (RA-L 2025).
fields.Key players: Industrial metrology vendors (not mapped here), academic calibration groups

fields.What it is: Legged robots and humanoids are not bolted to the ground: their base is a free 6-DoF body that moves only through contact forces. Centroidal dynamics summarizes the whole robot by its center of mass and momentum, which makes balance and jumping tractable. Optimal control libraries plan whole-body motions with these models.
fields.Prerequisites: Rigid-body dynamics; differential IK; optimization
fields.Frontier state 2026: Whole-body trajectory optimization and MPC (Crocoddyl, built on Pinocchio) handle multi-contact plans; in 2025-26 these models are often combined with RL tracking policies on low-cost humanoids such as Unitree G1.
fields.Key players: LAAS-CNRS / Heriot-Watt (Edinburgh Centre for Robotics) / Inria Willow (Crocoddyl), Unitree, Berkeley

fields.What it is: Contacts (feet, fingers, collisions) make dynamics discontinuous: forces appear suddenly. Simulators approximate contact with solvers or soft penalties. Differentiable simulators also return gradients of the outcome with respect to actions or parameters, for optimization and system identification.
fields.Prerequisites: Rigid-body dynamics; autodiff/JAX or PyTorch; GPUs
fields.Frontier state 2026: MuJoCo Warp (DeepMind + NVIDIA, Newton project) runs MuJoCo on GPUs; its README says differentiability is not yet available (tracked in issue #500). DiffMJX (2025) shows hard-contact gradients are biased and proposes fixes. Gradient quality through contact is still an open problem.
fields.Key players: Google DeepMind, NVIDIA, academic groups (DiffMJX: Paulus, Geist, Martius et al.)

fields.What it is: Retargeting converts human motion capture or video into joint trajectories for a robot with different proportions and joint limits. It is solved with IK plus constraints against foot sliding and self-collision. The result is the reference motion that RL tracking policies learn to imitate.
fields.Prerequisites: Differential IK; URDF/MJCF; motion-capture formats
fields.Frontier state 2026: GMR (2025) shows retargeting quality directly limits policy robustness and supports 15+ humanoids including Unitree G1 and Berkeley Humanoid Lite; BeyondMimic trains dynamic skills (cartwheels, sprints) from retargeted LAFAN1 data.
fields.Key players: Stanford (C. Karen Liu), UC Berkeley (Sreenath), Unitree

fields.What it is: Static balance keeps the centre of mass over supporting feet. Dynamic balance also depends on momentum and contact forces; a support polygon alone cannot guarantee a moving robot will stay upright.
fields.Prerequisites: Forces; torque; centre of mass
fields.Frontier state 2026: ZMP and contact feasibility remain useful abstractions but depend on contact and model assumptions. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: MIT Underactuated Robotics

fields.What it is: A gait describes when each foot touches the ground and when it swings. Phase offsets and duty factors turn the same legs into walking, trotting or bounding patterns.
fields.Prerequisites: Trigonometry; foot trajectories
fields.Frontier state 2026: Contact timing and smooth transitions matter as much as a visually plausible repeated animation. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: Stanford Robotics Club; Petoi; MIT

fields.What it is: Simplified models replace many joints with a mass and a small number of contacts. The linear inverted pendulum approximates walking, while a spring-loaded inverted pendulum models bouncing and running.
fields.Prerequisites: Differential equations; numerical integration
fields.Frontier state 2026: LIPM and SLIP expose useful structure but omit joint limits, impacts and much full-body dynamics. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: MIT Underactuated Robotics

fields.What it is: A central pattern generator is a coupled oscillator that produces rhythmic commands. Feedback can reset its phase when feet touch down, rather than replaying a fixed animation regardless of contact.
fields.Prerequisites: Gait phases; oscillator equations
fields.Frontier state 2026: Biologically inspired rhythm generation is not by itself a guarantee of balance or terrain robustness. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: EPFL BioRob

fields.What it is: A biped repeatedly moves its support from one foot to the other. ZMP preview and capture-point ideas choose body motion and steps that help keep the robot from falling.
fields.Prerequisites: Reduced-order models; feedback control; linear algebra
fields.Frontier state 2026: Classical walking remains an interpretable baseline; uneven contacts and model errors challenge flat-ground assumptions. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: MIT Underactuated Robotics

nodes.name: Model predictive control for legged robots

fields.What it is: MPC repeatedly predicts a short future and optimizes contact forces or motions. Convex approximations can make this fast when contact timing is already chosen.
fields.Prerequisites: Optimization; rigid-body dynamics; contact constraints
fields.Frontier state 2026: Convex MPC is not the same as solving arbitrary contact discovery; switched and nonlinear tools support richer models. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: MIT Biomimetics; ETH Robotic Systems Lab

fields.What it is: Whole-body control coordinates joints, body posture and contact forces together. It resolves competing tasks while respecting friction and actuator limits.
fields.Prerequisites: Robot Jacobians; inverse dynamics; optimization
fields.Frontier state 2026: Task hierarchies and optimal-control solvers trade tracking quality against feasibility and computation. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: LAAS-CNRS; Stack of Tasks; ETH

fields.What it is: Reinforcement learning trains a policy by rewarding useful movement in simulation. Domain randomization varies friction, masses and delays so the policy is less tied to one simulated world.
fields.Prerequisites: Python; neural networks; gait basics; feedback control
fields.Frontier state 2026: legged_gym is a historical Isaac Gym baseline; current Isaac Lab and MuJoCo Playground offer newer workflows. Simulation success alone does not establish hardware transfer. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: ETH; NVIDIA Isaac Lab; Google DeepMind

fields.What it is: Leg geometry and transmission choices change reach, force capability and impact behaviour. Proprioceptive actuation uses joint-side feedback to control interaction; this node focuses on mechanical trade-offs, not drive electronics.
fields.Prerequisites: Linkage kinematics; torque; basic CAD
fields.Frontier state 2026: Low inertia and backdrivability help contact control, but torque, heat and structural margins still constrain a design. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: Stanford Robotics Club; MIT Biomimetics

fields.What it is: Perceptive walking uses terrain observations to adapt foot placement or body motion. Delayed or missing depth data can make an otherwise capable gait unsafe.
fields.Prerequisites: Gaits; feedback; depth images; RL or MPC
fields.Frontier state 2026: Parkour and recent predictive perception work connect terrain sensing to low-level control; benchmark terrain and sensor faults rather than claiming universal all-terrain ability. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: Extreme Parkour authors; ETH Robotic Systems Lab; STEP and "Watch Your Step" humanoid authors (arXiv 2026)

fields.What it is: Recovery turns a fallen configuration into a stable standing pose. It needs contact-aware motions and a safe decision about when normal walking should resume.
fields.Prerequisites: Contact dynamics; joint limits; RL basics
fields.Frontier state 2026: ANYmal research demonstrated learned recovery, but generalization to arbitrary falls, obstacles and damaged hardware is not established. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: ETH Robotic Systems Lab

fields.What it is: Rotors produce thrust and moments that control a flying body. Cascaded rate, attitude and position loops separate fast stabilization from slower movement commands.
fields.Prerequisites: Rigid-body rotations; PID; forces and torque
fields.Frontier state 2026: PX4 documents controller architecture; this is flight stabilization, not aerial mapping or path planning. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: PX4; Bitcraze

fields.What it is: Wheel-legged robots can roll for efficiency and step when terrain demands it. The controller must coordinate rolling constraints, contact forces and transitions between modes.
fields.Prerequisites: Wheeled kinematics; legged contact dynamics; MPC or RL
fields.Frontier state 2026: Recent hybrid work couples rolling, stepping and body interaction; many papers use platform-specific assets rather than a universal controller. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: OmniQuad authors (arXiv 2610.38502); KYON authors (arXiv 2606.30243); ETH Robotic Systems Lab (OCS2)

fields.What it is: Retargeting converts human motion to a robot with different joints and proportions. A tracking policy then learns physically possible whole-body movement rather than directly replaying impossible joint angles.
fields.Prerequisites: Robot kinematics; motion data; RL; contact dynamics
fields.Frontier state 2026: DeepMimic is foundational; OmniH2O and RSS 2025 ASAP address robot motion tracking and deployment mismatch. Human video does not automatically yield safe robot motions. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: DeepMimic authors (UC Berkeley, UBC); OmniH2O authors; ASAP authors (RSS 2025); UC Berkeley HybridRobotics (BeyondMimic whole_body_tracking)

fields.What it is: Agile locomotion includes rapid jumps, dynamic obstacle crossing and fast contact changes. It combines precise timing, perception and control rather than just increasing walking speed.
fields.Prerequisites: Perceptive walking; RL; contact dynamics; recovery
fields.Frontier state 2026: Extreme Parkour reports impressive bounded course performance; safe extrapolation beyond training obstacles remains an open question. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: Extreme Parkour authors; ASAP authors

fields.What it is: Loco-manipulation coordinates balance and stepping while the robot interacts with an object. The focus here is how object forces and carried mass affect locomotion, not general grasp perception.
fields.Prerequisites: Whole-body control; contact dynamics; stability
fields.Frontier state 2026: OmniH2O and recent visual humanoid work connect whole-body skills and interaction, but long-horizon robustness needs careful evaluation. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: OmniH2O authors; recent humanoid research teams

fields.What it is: Cross-embodiment learning aims to reuse movement knowledge across bodies with different proportions or joints. A shared policy still needs a representation of each robot and careful testing on unseen bodies.
fields.Prerequisites: RL locomotion; robot morphology; motion representations
fields.Frontier state 2026: Recent generalist and rapid-adaptation preprints propose broader reuse; transfer across many real bodies remains a research question, not a turnkey low-cost platform. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
fields.Key players: Generalist humanoid and quadruped adaptation researchers

fields.What it is: A gripper is the tool at the end of an arm. Parallel jaws pinch, suction uses a pressure difference, and soft fingers bend around objects.
fields.Prerequisites: Basic forces; safe actuator operation
fields.Frontier state 2026: Match geometry and material to objects before adding learning; no universal gripper handles every surface. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: MIT manipulation course; industrial gripper designers

fields.What it is: Contact forces and friction determine whether an object slips. Form closure blocks motion geometrically; force closure uses frictional contacts to resist disturbances.
fields.Prerequisites: Vectors; moments; linear algebra
fields.Frontier state 2026: Friction models help explain failures but uncertain surface properties limit predictions on hardware. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: Lynch and Park; MIT Robot Locomotion Group

fields.What it is: A pick-and-place system finds an object, chooses a grasp, moves the arm, and releases it at a destination. Each stage must use consistent coordinates and recover when a grasp fails.
fields.Prerequisites: Coordinate frames; basic inverse kinematics; gripper safety
fields.Frontier state 2026: Reliable recovery and repeatable evaluation matter more than a single successful video. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: MIT; MoveIt community

fields.What it is: Teleoperation lets a person move an arm through a leader arm or another input device. Recording camera images and joint motion produces examples for imitation learning.
fields.Prerequisites: Joint limits; calibration; timestamps; emergency stop
fields.Frontier state 2026: The 2026 M3-Tele preprint studies synchronized multimodal demonstration collection and compliant whole-body teleoperation. Dataset quality, synchronized cameras and operator ergonomics constrain useful demonstrations; ALOHA 2 improves collection hardware. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: Hugging Face LeRobot; ALOHA 2 team

fields.What it is: A grasp detector predicts where a gripper could hold an object from an image or point cloud. A good grasp score does not guarantee the arm can reach it without collisions.
fields.Prerequisites: Point clouds; camera calibration; grasp mechanics
fields.Frontier state 2026: GraspNet supplies a benchmark and Contact-GraspNet predicts 6D grasps; clutter, sensor gaps and execution remain limitations. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: GraspNet team; NVIDIA Contact-GraspNet

fields.What it is: Pose estimation finds an object position and orientation relative to a camera. The robot transforms that estimate into its own coordinates to approach the object.
fields.Prerequisites: Rigid transforms; camera intrinsics; RGB-D data
fields.Frontier state 2026: FoundationPose supports pose estimation and tracking; symmetry, occlusion and calibration still complicate grasp execution. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: NVIDIA FoundationPose team

fields.What it is: Motion generation finds joint movements that avoid the table and other obstacles. It must check the arm links and attached objects, not just the gripper.
fields.Prerequisites: Inverse kinematics; collision geometry; coordinate frames
fields.Frontier state 2026: MoveIt 2 integrates planning and execution; cuRobo offers GPU-accelerated motion generation, with hardware and model requirements. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: MoveIt maintainers; NVIDIA cuRobo

fields.What it is: Compliance makes an arm yield instead of pushing rigidly against an obstacle. Impedance control acts like a virtual spring and damper, useful when inserting a peg or following a surface.
fields.Prerequisites: Dynamics; feedback control; force limits; contact mechanics
fields.Frontier state 2026: M3-Tele (2026 preprint) explicitly combines contact-force feedback and tactile adaptation. Insertion needs contact-aware feedback and safe limits; a position-only hobby arm is not a torque-controlled research arm. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: MIT; robosuite community

fields.What it is: Two arms can hold and manipulate an object together. Their motions must coordinate so they do not collide or pull against each other.
fields.Prerequisites: Single-arm manipulation; synchronization; shared frames
fields.Frontier state 2026: DECO (ICML 2026) studies bimanual visual, proprioceptive and tactile policy conditioning. ALOHA 2 improves bimanual demonstration hardware; coordinated contact and robustness remain difficult. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: ALOHA 2 team; Stanford

fields.What it is: A mobile manipulator combines an arm with a moving base. The base must stop in a place from which the arm can safely reach and manipulate an object.
fields.Prerequisites: Arm planning; base localization; safety zones
fields.Frontier state 2026: M3-Tele (2026 preprint) extends whole-body teleoperation toward compliant contact-rich interaction. Mobile ALOHA demonstrates whole-body imitation; deployment in changing rooms still requires robust perception and recovery. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: Stanford Mobile ALOHA team

fields.What it is: Tactile sensors measure what happens where a finger touches an object. Camera-based gel sensors turn small surface deformations into images that can reveal contact and slip.
fields.Prerequisites: Image processing; contact mechanics; sensor mounting
fields.Frontier state 2026: DECO (ICML 2026) reports a tactile adapter for bimanual manipulation; results are task-specific, not universal touch robustness. Touch complements vision during occlusion; calibration, gel wear and generalization across objects remain challenges. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: GelSight; tactile robotics community

fields.What it is: Cloth and cables change shape while the robot moves them. Unlike a rigid block, they cannot be described by one position and orientation.
fields.Prerequisites: Grasping; image processing; contact; learning basics
fields.Frontier state 2026: Cloth Funnels uses dynamic actions to improve cloth configuration; generalizing across materials and folds remains difficult. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: Columbia Cloth Funnels team

fields.What it is: In-hand manipulation changes an object pose while it stays between several fingers. The controller must repeatedly manage which fingers touch, roll or slide.
fields.Prerequisites: Contact mechanics; multi-joint control; reinforcement learning
fields.Frontier state 2026: STAR (2026 preprint) explores sparse tactile representations for dexterous vision-tactile-language-action policies. LEAP Hand makes research hardware more accessible; contact-rich sim-to-real transfer and reliable sensing remain bottlenecks. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: CMU LEAP Hand team

fields.What it is: An arm can move objects by pushing, sliding or pivoting without holding them. These actions exploit contact with the table or a wall.
fields.Prerequisites: Friction; rigid-body dynamics; feedback control
fields.Frontier state 2026: Contact mode changes make planning difficult; controlled pushing remains a useful complement to grasping. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: MIT; Lynch and Park

fields.What it is: Task planning chooses steps such as opening a drawer before picking an item. Motion planning checks that each step can actually be executed by the arm.
fields.Prerequisites: State machines; symbolic search; collision-free arm planning
fields.Frontier state 2026: Combining symbolic choices with continuous geometry and recovery remains difficult; language plans need executable checks. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: MIT manipulation course; planning research community

fields.What it is: Open-vocabulary systems accept descriptions beyond a fixed list of objects. Affordances describe useful actions, such as pulling a handle, rather than just recognizing its name.
fields.Prerequisites: Vision-language models; geometry; manipulation planning
fields.Frontier state 2026: VoxPoser builds value maps and ReKep uses relational keypoint constraints; physical grounding and failure detection remain essential. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: VoxPoser team; ReKep team

fields.What it is: A vision-language-action model maps camera images and instructions to robot actions. Generalist policies aim to reuse experience across tasks, but still need the right action format and robot calibration.
fields.Prerequisites: Imitation learning; datasets; arm interfaces; evaluation
fields.Frontier state 2026: STAR (2026 preprint) adds touch to the vision-language-action recipe for dexterous manipulation. OpenVLA, Octo and pi0 demonstrate transferable policies; their published results do not guarantee reliable transfer to a low-cost arm. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: OpenVLA team; Octo team; Physical Intelligence

fields.What it is: A motor supplies motion; a joint actuator packages that motor with bearings, transmission and structure. Compare brushed servomotors, steppers and brushless motors by torque-speed behaviour, mass and how they mount, rather than by their command protocol.
fields.Prerequisites: Basic forces and units; Electronics fundamentals for robots; Smart servos & serial actuator buses for powered tests.
fields.Frontier state 2026: Established design choices, not a winner-takes-all technology. Current integration work combines motor, reducer, bearings and thermal path; this node excludes FOC firmware and serial-bus setup.
fields.Key players: MIT robotics teaching; maxon; Open Dynamic Robot Initiative

nodes.name: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty

fields.What it is: Sizing means checking whether an actuator can move the actual load repeatedly, not just once at peak torque. Include gravity, acceleration, gear ratio, reflected rotor inertia and heat during the duty cycle.
fields.Prerequisites: Electric actuator architectures: mechanical trade-offs; basic algebra and free-body diagrams; motor datasheet units.
fields.Frontier state 2026: Continuous and peak ratings remain different constraints. maxon documents temperature-dependent motor data; real winding temperature and assembly heat transfer must be measured rather than inferred from a catalogue peak.
fields.Key players: maxon; MIT Modern Robotics teaching

fields.What it is: Gears trade speed for torque while changing direction or packaging. A planetary train places smaller planet gears around a sun gear; housing, tooth count, backlash and bearing alignment affect whether it works well.
fields.Prerequisites: Electric actuator architectures: mechanical trade-offs; basic ratios; CAD sketches.
fields.Frontier state 2026: Planetary and spur gearing are established. Printed teaching models explain reduction but their friction, tooth strength and backlash do not establish industrial actuator performance.
fields.Key players: Harmonic Drive planetary products; MIT machine-design teaching

fields.What it is: An eccentric input makes a lobed disc move around a ring of pins. An output mechanism removes that wobble to obtain slow rotation; tolerances, bearing loads and disc balancing matter as much as the theoretical ratio.
fields.Prerequisites: Spur and planetary gear trains; Bearings, structures and printed load paths; CAD and design for manufacture of robot joints.
fields.Frontier state 2026: Nabtesco documents a two-stage RV mechanism. Student printed cycloidal reducers are useful experiments, not drop-in substitutes for precision commercial reducers.
fields.Key players: Nabtesco; MIT machine-design teaching

fields.What it is: A wave generator flexes a thin toothed cup into an oval so it engages a rigid ring. A small tooth-count difference gives large reduction, but flexspline fatigue, elastic twist and manufacturing accuracy constrain the design.
fields.Prerequisites: Spur and planetary gear trains; Bearings, structures and printed load paths; material elasticity.
fields.Frontier state 2026: Harmonic Drive explains metal flexspline and wave-generator operation. Vendor zero-backlash claims do not mean infinite stiffness or that a printed educational flexspline has the same rating.
fields.Key players: Harmonic Drive; MIT machine-design teaching

fields.What it is: Belts and wrapped cables move torque away from the motor, reducing moving mass at a joint. Belt tension, pulley alignment and cable preload set stiffness, slip and usable travel; a capstan is not simply an unlimited-rotation cable pulley.
fields.Prerequisites: Spur and planetary gear trains; Bearings, structures and printed load paths; safe handling of tensioned elements.
fields.Frontier state 2026: MIT design notes discuss belt tension and capstan termination; ODRI provides pulley-based actuator assembly examples. Low apparent backlash still needs load-reversal and tension-loss testing.
fields.Key players: Open Dynamic Robot Initiative; MIT machine-design teaching

nodes.name: Lead screws, ball screws and linear joint packaging

fields.What it is: A rotating screw turns motor motion into linear travel. Lead screws slide while ball screws use rolling balls; lead, guide alignment, buckling, preload and backdriving determine whether a linear joint is suitable.
fields.Prerequisites: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty; Bearings, structures and printed load paths.
fields.Frontier state 2026: MIT design notes contrast sliding and rolling screws and explain over-constrained guide alignment. Do not assume every screw self-locks; gravity loads need an independent retention assessment.
fields.Key players: MIT machine-design teaching; linear-motion component designers

nodes.name: Linkages, cams and parallel mechanism design

fields.What it is: A linkage constrains several connected pieces to make a useful path; cams shape motion through a profile. Serial, closed-loop and parallel arrangements trade reach, stiffness and assembly complexity, while singular configurations can jam or amplify loads.
fields.Prerequisites: Basic geometry and forces; CAD sketches. Full inverse kinematics belongs in Kinematics & dynamics.
fields.Frontier state 2026: MIT mechanism teaching grounds joint primitives and open/closed chains. DLR uses shaped cams in variable-stiffness joints; the focus here is geometry and load paths rather than a general motion-planning node.
fields.Key players: MIT robotics teaching; DLR

nodes.name: Tendon routing, antagonism and underactuated mechanisms

fields.What it is: Tendons pull but do not push, so routing, pretension and a return spring or opposing tendon determine movement. Underactuation uses fewer motors than joints, making the mechanical coupling useful but also harder to predict.
fields.Prerequisites: Timing-belt and capstan transmissions; Linkages, cams and parallel mechanism design; Grasp mechanics for hand applications.
fields.Frontier state 2026: RSS 2025 RUKA and RSS 2024 pneumatic-arm research expose routing and low-distal-mass trade-offs. This node studies transmission and coupling, not another gripper-design or dexterous-policy node.
fields.Key players: RUKA authors; DLR; RSS pneumatic-arm authors

fields.What it is: Backdrivability means an external load can move the actuator backwards. Transparency describes how little extra inertia and friction the mechanism adds; low gear ratio helps but does not by itself prove low friction or safe contact.
fields.Prerequisites: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty; Spur and planetary gear trains; guarded test fixtures.
fields.Frontier state 2026: Modern Robotics explains squared gear-ratio effects on reflected inertia. MIT Cheetah actuator research grounds low-ratio design; transparency and passive safety must be measured, not inferred from current sensing.
fields.Key players: MIT Biomimetic Robotics; Modern Robotics authors

fields.What it is: A deliberate spring between drive and output stores energy and makes output force observable through spring deflection. The spring also introduces resonance and limits bandwidth, so stiffness selection and mechanical stops are design decisions.
fields.Prerequisites: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty; Backdrivability, friction and mechanical transparency; elementary spring forces.
fields.Frontier state 2026: DLR references distinguish intentional series elasticity from incidental gearbox compliance. Elasticity trades shock tolerance and energy storage against deflection and dynamics; it is not a universal improvement.
fields.Key players: DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics; compliant-actuator researchers

fields.What it is: Variable-stiffness hardware changes its physical spring behaviour rather than merely changing a controller gain. Cams, moving lever arms or opposing spring-loaded motors can adjust how strongly a joint resists displacement.
fields.Prerequisites: Series-elastic actuator mechanics; Linkages, cams and parallel mechanism design; Control fundamentals for powered experiments.
fields.Frontier state 2026: DLR David documents antagonism, BAVS and Floating Spring Joint concepts. The research question is useful stiffness range versus mass, energy and complexity, not an unsupported claim of new 2026 adoption.
fields.Key players: DLR; authors of the variable-stiffness actuator design review

nodes.name: Bearings, structures and printed load paths

fields.What it is: Bearings guide rotation while the surrounding frame carries loads into the base. Shaft support, fits, fasteners and print orientation matter: a strong motor cannot rescue a flexible bracket or a bearing seat that creeps.
fields.Prerequisites: Basic forces, moments and material elasticity; measuring tools; safe fabrication induction.
fields.Frontier state 2026: SKF distinguishes bearing families; Prusa explains print-aware modeling. Printed prototypes need measured stiffness and fit checks; catalogue material strength is not a complete printed-part rating.
fields.Key players: SKF; Prusa Research; ODRI hardware authors

nodes.name: CAD and design for manufacture of robot joints

fields.What it is: Parametric CAD describes parts using dimensions and constraints so changes remain consistent. Robot design also needs assemblies, tolerance allowances, fastener access, serviceable cable paths and a believable mass model before fabrication.
fields.Prerequisites: Basic geometry; introductory mechanical drawing; Bearings, structures and printed load paths for loaded parts.
fields.Frontier state 2026: FreeCAD provides parametric modeling and assembly capabilities; onshape-to-robot exports robot descriptions. CAD export is a starting model, not proof of correct inertia, friction or manufacturing tolerances.
fields.Key players: FreeCAD contributors; onshape-to-robot maintainers; Prusa Research

fields.What it is: Pressurized liquid or air drives a piston or contracting muscle. Force depends on pressure and effective area; seals, hoses, compressibility, pumps or compressors and leakage change the complete system, not just the actuator.
fields.Prerequisites: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty; elementary pressure and fluid units; supervised pressure-system safety.
fields.Frontier state 2026: RSS 2024 demonstrates a pneumatic-muscle tendon arm. Boston Dynamics retired hydraulic Atlas for an electric successor in 2024; that is one platform decision, not proof that hydraulics are obsolete.
fields.Key players: Festo; RSS pneumatic-arm authors; Boston Dynamics

nodes.name: Soft pneumatic actuators and compliant-body fabrication

fields.What it is: An elastomer chamber bends or extends when inflated because its geometry constrains expansion unevenly. Molds, wall thickness, reinforcement and repeatable sealing are the mechanism, rather than a separate rigid gearbox.
fields.Prerequisites: Hydraulic and pneumatic transmission mechanics; CAD and design for manufacture of robot joints; materials handling induction.
fields.Frontier state 2026: The Harvard-origin Soft Robotics Toolkit documents PneuNets design, fabrication and testing. Reliable pressure-angle behaviour and fatigue remain tasks to measure; do not extrapolate a single bending video into industrial durability.
fields.Key players: Harvard Biodesign Lab; Soft Robotics Toolkit contributors

nodes.name: Artificial muscles: electrohydraulic and smart-material actuation

fields.What it is: Artificial muscles change shape directly using materials or internal fluids rather than a rotating motor. Electrohydraulic pouches such as HASEL and HALVE combine electrical attraction with fluid displacement; shape-memory and piezoelectric approaches occupy different force, stroke and thermal regimes.
fields.Prerequisites: Soft pneumatic actuators and compliant-body fabrication; material mechanics; specialist high-voltage safety before any energized electrohydraulic work.
fields.Frontier state 2026: The 2024 HALVE paper reduces voltage relative to prior electrohydraulic actuators, but its reported 1100 V is not hobby-safe low voltage. Other smart-material families are acknowledged here, not claimed comprehensively surveyed or ready for procurement. A 2025 SMA microactuator paper demonstrates thermally controlled folding and magnetic latching; a PNAS origami arm demonstrates magnetic actuation. These are research-specific mechanisms, not interchangeable muscles.
fields.Key players: ETH Zurich Soft Robotics Lab; HALVE paper authors

nodes.name: Integrated legged and humanoid joint co-design

fields.What it is: A useful leg or humanoid joint balances torque, speed, mass, cooling, travel, impact tolerance and maintenance. Quasi-direct drive uses a relatively low reduction ratio with a torque-dense motor; parallel links or remote drives offer other packaging trade-offs.
fields.Prerequisites: Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty; Bearings, structures and printed load paths; Backdrivability, friction and mechanical transparency; BLDC motor control & field-oriented control (FOC) for powered drives.
fields.Frontier state 2026: ODRI exposes module assembly and test stands; ToddlerBot documents maintainable hardware and 2025/2026 releases. Atlas 2026 manufacturer statements give ecosystem context, not public internal actuator specs or independently verified deployment performance.
fields.Key players: Open Dynamic Robot Initiative; Stanford ToddlerBot team; MIT Biomimetic Robotics; Boston Dynamics

fields.What it is: A camera turns 3D points into 2D pixels through a lens. The pinhole model, focal length, principal point and lens distortion describe this mapping, so code can go from pixels back to rays in the world.
fields.Prerequisites: Linear algebra (matrices, homogeneous coordinates); Python/NumPy
fields.Frontier state 2026: Mature theory; still the base of every 3D perception pipeline. Learned models (VGGT, Depth Anything 3) now also predict camera parameters from images. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: Textbook authors (Szeliski; Hartley & Zisserman; Corke); OpenCV community

fields.What it is: Calibration measures a camera's internal parameters and where it sits relative to the robot. You show a checkerboard or ChArUco board from many angles and solve for the parameters; hand-eye calibration links camera frame and gripper frame.
fields.Prerequisites: Camera models; rigid transforms
fields.Frontier state 2026: Standard tooling exists (OpenCV, ROS camera_calibration, Kalibr for camera-IMU). Low-cost arm demos such as Google's SO-101 pointing sample still rely on a ChArUco homography step. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: ETH Zurich ASL (Kalibr); OpenCV; ROS image_pipeline maintainers

fields.What it is: Before deep learning, robots found edges, corners, colors and keypoints with hand-written filters. Matching keypoints between images gives motion and 3D structure, and simple color thresholds are still the fastest way to get a first demo.
fields.Prerequisites: Python; arrays; basic linear algebra
fields.Frontier state 2026: Still used for fast, explainable baselines and in SLAM front-ends; learned matchers compete for hard cases. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: OpenCV; university perception courses (UMD ENPM673)

fields.What it is: Fiducials are printed black-and-white square codes that software detects reliably and uses to compute the 6D pose of the tag. They are the quickest way to give a robot accurate object or camera positions without training a model.
fields.Prerequisites: Camera calibration
fields.Frontier state 2026: Mature and widely used for ground truth, calibration and docking; AprilTag 3 library is the open reference. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
fields.Key players: University of Michigan APRIL Lab; OpenCV ArUco module

lesson.summary: A fiducial marker is a printed, machine-readable pattern that helps a camera identify a known object and estimate its pose.
lesson.lesson_md:
## In one sentence
A fiducial marker is a printed, machine-readable pattern that helps a camera identify a known object and estimate its pose.

## Why it matters for us
A student can print a square marker, place it near a cube, and let a webcam report its ID and corners. The robot can use those corners to estimate where the marker is relative to the camera, then transform that pose into its arm base frame. A unique tag ID is often easier to detect than an unmarked object, especially in a controlled demo or lab setup.

## How it works
The detector finds square candidates, checks their black border and binary code, corrects for rotation, and returns an identifier with four image corners. AprilTag and ArUco are related but distinct marker families. OpenCV 4.13.0's `ArucoDetector` supports predefined ArUco dictionaries and AprilTag families. Pose estimation additionally needs camera intrinsics and the marker's physical side length; without a known length, image size alone cannot provide distance in meters.

## Key terms
- **Dictionary**: the set of allowed marker codes a detector searches.
- **Pose**: an object's position and orientation.
- **Camera intrinsics**: focal lengths and optical center, which map camera rays to image pixels.
- **Distortion coefficients**: values that model lens warping.
- **Corner coordinates**: pixel locations, not robot-world coordinates; a printed border and contrast help detection, while glare, blur, occlusion, or a tiny image can cause misses.

## Before / after
Before markers, a program may search an image for a generic object and struggle to distinguish it from background clutter. After a tag is detected, it can report a known ID and a geometric target. This is like adding a unique key to an otherwise anonymous record: the identifier is reliable only if the right dictionary and calibration are used.

## Try it in an afternoon
Generate or print one AprilTag, calibrate a webcam, and draw returned corners and ID on each frame. Measure the printed side length as 0.10 m, then estimate pose using the camera matrix. Test at two distances and turn the tag through 90°; verify that the ID remains stable and the pose changes sensibly. Use OpenCV's current 4.x docs, not the old 4.0.1 calibration page.
