fields.Key players: Advanced Machine Intelligence (Paris), Meta (V-JEPA 2), NVIDIA, Google DeepMind
fields.Project ideas: Natural follow-up to the AI Lab's JEPA bootcamp: train a small latent world model on our SO-101 dataset and use it for planning
fields.What it is: Models that learn to predict how the world will evolve (e.g. the next video frames, or an abstract representation of them) and use that prediction to choose actions. The bet: a robot that can 'imagine' consequences generalizes better.
fields.Best resources: V-JEPA 2 paper; recent world-action-model papers on arXiv
fields.Frontier state 2026: Hottest research direction of 2026: 'world action models' unify video prediction and action, JEPA-style latent world models are being plugged into VLAs. Paris has a major player: Advanced Machine Intelligence, which raised close to €890M in 2026.
fields.Prerequisites: Self-supervised learning, video models, JEPA concepts

fields.Key players: Hugging Face, NVIDIA (Isaac Teleop), Bleu Robotics
fields.Project ideas: Build a lab data-collection station and publish a dataset on the Hub; VR teleop for SO-101
fields.What it is: The tooling to let a human drive a robot (leader arm, VR headset, phone) while recording synchronized video and joint data. In modern robotics, data is the bottleneck, so whoever collects good data fast wins.
fields.Frontier state 2026: Standardized dataset formats (LeRobotDataset on the HF Hub) and cheap leader/follower arms. Startups compete on deployment speed: e.g. Bleu Robotics claims new tasks from \~10 demonstrations.
fields.Prerequisites: Python, cameras, serial/USB communication basics

fields.Key players: Academic labs; several Chinese robotics teams
fields.Project ideas: Turn smartphone videos of lab members into SO-101 training data
fields.What it is: Using videos of humans doing tasks (YouTube, egocentric cameras) to train robots, instead of expensive robot demonstrations. Requires detecting hand poses and translating them into robot motions.
fields.Frontier state 2026: 'Data engines' that retarget human hand motions onto robots and composite robot arms into videos measurably improve real-robot success; egocentric-video pretraining is a growing family of models.
fields.Prerequisites: Computer vision (pose estimation, segmentation), imitation learning

fields.Key players: Stanford (ACT/ALOHA), Columbia/TRI (Diffusion Policy), Hugging Face LeRobot
fields.Project ideas: Train an SO-101 to sort objects by color; pick-and-place with distractors; benchmark ACT vs Diffusion Policy with 20/50/100 demos
fields.What it is: Teach a robot by showing it: a human performs the task (usually by teleoperation), the robot records camera images and joint positions, and a neural network learns to map what it sees to what it should do. It's supervised learning where the labels are actions.
fields.Best resources: LeRobot docs + tutorials; ACT and Diffusion Policy papers
fields.Frontier state 2026: Mature workhorse. ACT and Diffusion Policy are the standard baselines; most teams now fine-tune a pretrained VLA instead of training from scratch. Open problem: generalization beyond the demonstrated setup.
fields.Prerequisites: PyTorch, basic CNNs/transformers. No control theory needed to start.

lesson.summary: Behavior cloning trains a robot policy to imitate actions recorded from a human or another controller.
lesson.lesson_md:
## In one sentence
Behavior cloning trains a robot policy to imitate actions recorded from a human or another controller.

## Why it matters for us
A student can teleoperate a SO-101 arm to pick up a cube and save camera images with joint positions. The training set becomes examples of “when the image and joint state looked like this, the operator chose these next actions.” A model learns a mapping from observations to actions. This is easier to start than writing every grasp rule by hand, but the model only sees what the demonstrations show.

## How it works
A dataset is split into episodes, each a time-ordered sequence of observations and actions. Behavior cloning minimizes the difference between the expert's action and the model's action for each observation. In ALOHA's ACT system, Action Chunking with Transformers predicts a sequence of actions instead of one step; the paper reports chunks of 90 joint-position steps and about 50 demonstrations per task. Chunking can smooth behavior but makes recovery from errors an important design question.

## Key terms
- **Demonstration**: a recorded example of the desired behavior.
- **Observation**: input such as camera frames and joint state.
- **Action**: a commanded joint position or motor target.
- **Policy**: a function that maps observations to actions.
- **Generalization**: success on new object positions, lighting, or starting poses not seen during training.

## Before / after
Before learning, a student hand-codes “if object is here, move the wrist there.” After behavior cloning, the student supplies examples and trains a policy. This resembles supervised learning for an API classifier, except the outputs affect a moving mechanism and a slightly wrong action can make the arm miss or collide. Evaluation must use fresh episodes, not just the training video.

## Try it in an afternoon
Record a small set of consistent pick demonstrations, split out held-out trials, and compare success rate across both sets. Plot frames and actions together to catch unsynchronized cameras. Start with low-payload objects and a simulation rollout; then use LeRobot's documented recording and rollout tools. Treat 50 episodes as a starting point from a particular tutorial, not a universal guarantee.

lesson.summary: The SO-101 is a low-cost six-joint robot arm designed for teleoperation and robot-learning experiments.
lesson.lesson_md:
## In one sentence
The SO-101 is a low-cost six-joint robot arm designed for teleoperation and robot-learning experiments.

## Why it matters for us
The SO-101 gives software students a tangible platform for connecting cameras, serial communication, joint calibration, and learned policies. LeRobot's current setup page describes a follower arm driven by six FEETECH STS3215 servos, plus a leader arm that a person moves by hand. A small tabletop task such as moving a cube makes datasets and robot actions visible without requiring an industrial manipulator.

## What it is made of / how it works
The arm has a base, shoulder, elbow, wrist joints, and a gripper. Each servo reports position and receives commands on an ID-addressed serial bus. The LeRobot docs list six STS3215 motors on the follower and distinct leader/follower gearing: leader ratios are 1/191 for base and elbow, 1/345 for shoulder lift, and 1/147 for wrist flex, wrist roll, and gripper. Calibration maps a motor's raw range to useful joint motion.

## Key terms
- **Follower**: the arm that reproduces received commands.
- **Leader**: the human-moved input device used to guide the follower.
- **Teleoperation**: remote control of a robot by a person.
- **Calibration**: mapping raw sensor or motor readings to meaningful positions.
- **Joint limit**: the safe mechanical range of a joint.

## Getting started
Assemble the arm with the official current guide, connect the motor bus, then follow LeRobot's setup and calibration instructions. On Linux a serial device may appear as `/dev/ttyACM0`, but its name depends on the machine. Use the official `lerobot-teleoperate` command with a follower and leader configuration, confirm the exact port and robot ID values reported by your system rather than copying another computer's device path, and test slow movement before recording. Keep the gripper clear of fingers and fragile objects during powered tests.

## Used in
The SO-101 appears in LeRobot's real-world imitation-learning tutorial, where teams record episodes, train policies, and run rollouts. It is also the hardware used in this pilot's assembly/teleoperation and SmolVLA projects. A successful hand-guided pick gives a baseline; a trained policy should then be measured on new object positions rather than judged from a single demonstration.

lesson.summary: The FEETECH STS3215 is a bus-controlled servo with a magnetic encoder and a gear train used in the SO-101 follower arm.
lesson.lesson_md:
## In one sentence
The FEETECH STS3215 is a bus-controlled servo with a magnetic encoder and a gear train used in the SO-101 follower arm.

## Why it matters for us
A robot's joint is not an abstract variable: it is moved by a motor that has voltage, torque, speed, position, and communication limits. The STS3215 is a concrete example. FEETECH specifies a 7.4 V nominal servo with a 6–7.4 V operating range; the manufacturer lists 19.5 kg·cm peak stall torque at 6 V, not at 7.4 V. Reading the test voltage alongside a torque number prevents a misleading comparison.

## What it is made of / how it works
The motor combines a DC motor, gears, a control board, and a 12-bit magnetic encoder. Twelve bits give 2¹² = 4096 distinguishable counts per turn. It uses TTL-level half-duplex asynchronous serial: the shared wire alternates between command and reply. Servos are addressed by IDs (manufacturer page lists 0–253), so several devices can share a bus if IDs are unique. The SO-101 follower uses six of these servos.

## Key terms
- **Stall torque**: torque measured while the output is prevented from turning; it is not continuous operating torque.
- **Half-duplex**: communication where data travels in both directions, but not simultaneously.
- **Daisy chain**: devices connected along one bus, with each device listening for its own ID.
- **Encoder resolution**: the count resolution, not a guarantee of equal absolute accuracy after calibration.

## Getting started
Read the official FEETECH product data, confirm the supply range, connect the correct bus interface, assign unique IDs, and use a current LeRobot setup guide for calibration. The manufacturer lists serial speeds from 38,400 bps to 1 Mbps and 360° operation over positions 0–4096. Do not infer that a continuous-rotation configuration is safe for a joint with mechanical stops.

## Used in
The STS3215 is used in the SO-101/LeRobot arm stack as the joint actuator. Its encoder feedback makes it possible to record joint state alongside camera data. The FEETECH page is the source for the electrical and protocol figures; the LeRobot documentation shows how the servo is configured as part of a complete robot rather than a standalone motor.

lesson.summary: The Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit is an NVIDIA edge-computing platform for running AI and robotics software near the robot.
lesson.lesson_md:
## In one sentence
The Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit is an NVIDIA edge-computing platform for running AI and robotics software near the robot.

## Why it matters for us
A robot often needs to process camera images without sending every frame to a remote server. The Jetson kit provides a small Linux computer with an NVIDIA GPU and interfaces for cameras and peripherals. NVIDIA's December 2024 Super announcement reported up to 67 sparse TOPS (trillions of operations per second), 8 GB LPDDR5 memory, 102 GB/s memory bandwidth, and selectable 7 W, 15 W, and 25 W module power modes.

## What it is made of / how it works
The developer kit combines a system-on-module with a carrier board, connectors, and software stack. TOPS is a peak AI-throughput measure, not a promise that every model runs at that speed. NVIDIA's same announcement reported 33 dense TOPS and 17 FP16 TFLOPs under its stated metrics, and reduced the kit price to $249 at the time. Price and availability change, so treat that figure as a dated announcement rather than a current quote.

## Key terms
- **Edge computing**: running inference on or near the robot.
- **RAM**: memory holding active programs and tensors.
- **Bandwidth**: how quickly data moves between memory and processors.
- **Power mode**: the module's power budget, which affects performance and heat; a model that fits in memory can still exceed latency or thermal limits.

## Getting started
Use NVIDIA's current Jetson Linux guide for supported software and the Jetson AI Lab tutorials for edge-AI workflows. Check camera interfaces, storage, cooling, and power supply before attaching the board to a robot. Benchmark the complete pipeline—camera capture, model inference, and actuator communication—rather than quoting TOPS alone.

## Used in
The kit can host ROS 2 nodes, camera processing, and smaller learned policies on a mobile robot or arm. It is a compute option, not an actuator controller: motor power and safety remain separate. NVIDIA's 2024 performance and price claims are useful for comparing that announced revision with a laptop or cloud machine, but verify the exact module and software version you buy.

lesson.summary: LeRobot is Hugging Face's open-source software toolkit for connecting robots to datasets, policies, training, and evaluation.
lesson.lesson_md:
## In one sentence
LeRobot is Hugging Face's open-source software toolkit for connecting robots to datasets, policies, training, and evaluation.

## Why it matters for us
A software student can use LeRobot to teleoperate an SO-101, record camera and joint data, train a policy, and replay it on the robot. It avoids writing every camera driver, dataset writer, and training script from scratch. The toolkit also provides a common interface across supported arms, so an experiment can focus on data quality and task design instead of inventing a new file format.

## What it is made of / how it works
The workflow has distinct commands: `lerobot-teleoperate` streams human input to a robot; `lerobot-record` saves episodes; `lerobot-train` fits a policy; and `lerobot-rollout` evaluates the policy. A dataset repository ID names a versioned collection of episodes. Each episode can include image observations, joint state, action targets, and a task description. Hardware configuration still matters: port names, robot IDs, camera names, and calibration must match the actual setup.

## Key terms
- **Dataset episode**: one time-ordered run of a task.
- **Policy**: a function that maps observations to actions.
- **Rollout**: running a policy in an environment.
- **Calibration**: aligning sensor values with physical positions.
- **Library**: reusable code that other programs can call.
- **Driver**: software that communicates with a specific device.

## Getting started
Install the current package using the official docs, follow the SO-101 setup, calibrate leader and follower, and run `lerobot-teleoperate`. Record only after you can move the follower smoothly. Start with a small local dataset and a few clearly labeled episodes; check that camera frames and joint state arrive at the same rate. Keep a note of the LeRobot version because command options change over time.

## Used in
The pilot's SO-101, demonstration-collection, ACT, and SmolVLA lessons all use LeRobot as the bridge between hardware and learning. It is maintained in the `huggingface/lerobot` repository, while the real-world robot tutorial documents an end-to-end workflow. The software can support an experiment, but it does not remove the need to inspect the robot, supervise motion, and evaluate on held-out trials.

lesson.summary: SmolVLA is a compact vision-language-action model that turns camera observations, robot state, and a text instruction into robot action chunks.
lesson.lesson_md:
## In one sentence
SmolVLA is a compact vision-language-action model that turns camera observations, robot state, and a text instruction into robot action chunks.

## Why it matters for us
A language-commanded arm makes the connection between modern AI and physical robotics concrete: “pick up the red block” must become a sequence of joint targets. Hugging Face reports that SmolVLA has 450 million parameters and accepts multi-camera RGB images, robot sensorimotor state, and natural-language instructions. Its output is continuous robot actions grouped into short chunks, not a paragraph explaining what to do.

## What it is made of / how it works
The model combines visual, language, and proprioceptive inputs, where proprioception means sensing the robot's own joint state. A learned policy predicts a short action horizon, which the runtime executes before requesting another prediction. The published training mix contains 487 curated SO-100 datasets, recorded at 30 frames per second, totaling about 10 million frames. Those numbers describe the reported training set, not a guarantee that a new task works from a handful of episodes.

## Key terms
- **VLA**: a vision-language-action model that maps visual and language context to physical actions.
- **Parameter**: a learned numeric weight in a model.
- **Action chunk**: several future control steps predicted together.
- **Proprioceptive state**: the robot's own measured configuration.
- **Instruction**: a description of intent; calibration and task data determine what the model can execute.

## Getting started
Use the current LeRobot SmolVLA docs and pretrained `lerobot/smolvla_base` checkpoint. Prepare a dataset with the camera names expected by the policy; the docs show a rename map and a training command with 20,000 steps. Begin with a known tabletop task, inspect a few episodes visually, and test the pretrained model in simulation before enabling hardware.

## Used in
SmolVLA is used in LeRobot's language-commanded arm project. The model is open-source and intended to run with accessible robot hardware, but inference cost depends on the machine, image resolution, and configuration. Compare the model's success on held-out positions with a simpler behavior-cloning baseline, and record the exact checkpoint and dataset revision.

fields.Key specs: Onboard operating system for connected autonomous vehicles and commercial fleet/mission integration; not synonymous with the entirely open PX4 project.
fields.Why it matters: Distinguishes an open upstream flight stack from commercial product layers.

fields.Price / access: Commercial/research system; price and student access unknown.
fields.Key specs: Drop-in logistics robot for singulation, loading and unloading; manufacturer advertises under-10-minute deployment and a 1 m² footprint.
fields.Why it matters: Commercial manipulation case study, not evidence of affordable student access.

fields.Price / access: Commercial/research system; price and student access unknown.
fields.Key specs: Compact handling platform for high-mix small objects; advertised 0.5 m² footprint.
fields.Why it matters: Shows how task scope and product packaging matter alongside learned perception.

nodes.name: TINAMU RMS Automated Robotic Monitoring System

fields.Price / access: Commercial/research system; price and student access unknown.
fields.Key specs: Indoor inventory monitoring platform combining automated drone navigation without GNSS with analytics.
fields.Why it matters: A real perception-to-operational-data workflow students could study in simplified simulation.

fields.Price / access: Commercial/research system; price and student access unknown.
fields.Key specs: Expressive bipedal entertainment robots trained in simulation with reinforcement learning; not human-shaped humanoids.
fields.Why it matters: A strong sim-to-real/character-animation case study; no public hardware purchase path is established.

fields.Price / access: AGPL-3.0 source; check commercial licensing requirements.
fields.Key specs: Computer-vision pretraining, fine-tuning and distillation framework. Repository lists AGPL-3.0 and commercial licensing guidance.
fields.Why it matters: Software-only entry point for improving visual representations using a team's own robot data.

fields.Price / access: Free source; inspect license and dependencies.
fields.Key specs: Local browser-based dataset curation, annotation and evaluation platform; repository lists Apache-2.0.
fields.Why it matters: Helps beginners inspect datasets before spending effort training robot policies.

fields.Price / access: Free source; inspect license and dependencies.
fields.Key specs: CPU volumetric mapping library with TSDF/ESDF representations and ROS integration; BSD-3-Clause.
fields.Why it matters: Connects 3D sensing to collision-aware motion planning. Historical ROS integration may require adaptation.

fields.Price / access: Free source; inspect license and dependencies.
fields.Key specs: Modular quadrotor simulator separates Unity rendering from dynamics, with sensor outputs and reinforcement-learning interfaces; MIT license.
fields.Why it matters: A software-first aerial robotics learning environment; not a new 2026 simulator release.

fields.Price / access: Free source; commercial support optional.
fields.Key specs: Open-source desktop robot simulator with physics, robot/sensor models and programming interfaces; official repository is Apache-2.0.
fields.Why it matters: Affordable full robot simulation before spending on hardware.

fields.Price / access: Public source; check license/dependencies for the selected language repository.
fields.Key specs: Programming-by-demonstration library collection for statistical learning, dynamical systems, geometry and optimal control; Matlab, C++ and Python versions have separate repositories.
fields.Why it matters: Small-data imitation-learning baselines complement neural VLA experiments.

fields.Price / access: unknown; contact supplier.
fields.Key specs: Autonomous mobile base plus collaborative manipulation and human interaction for care/research/professional tasks.
fields.Why it matters: Combines navigation and manipulation in real human environments.

fields.Price / access: unknown; contact supplier.
fields.Key specs: Mobile manipulation system intended to automate material transport in laboratories.
fields.Why it matters: A concrete laboratory logistics and mobile-manipulation use case.

fields.Price / access: unknown; configurable commercial system.
fields.Key specs: Modular laboratory robot workstation with liquid handling and robotic arms for pipetting/gripping and labware transport.
fields.Why it matters: Shows industrial-scale workflow repeatability rather than unconstrained general manipulation.

fields.Price / access: unknown; professional system and trained operation.
fields.Key specs: Collision-tolerant confined-space inspection drone with pilot assistance and interchangeable sensing payload options.
fields.Why it matters: Inspection combines perception, localization and robust mechanical protection.

fields.Price / access: unknown; regulated clinical system, not student experimentation hardware.
fields.Key specs: Robotic surgery system for minimally invasive procedures, designed to fit existing operating-room workflows and compatible technologies.
fields.Why it matters: Illustrates teleoperation, usability and safety constraints.

fields.Price / access: unknown; commercial agricultural implement.
fields.Key specs: AI-guided tractor-mounted ultra-high-precision spraying implement detecting crops/weeds plant by plant; not a self-driving vehicle claim.
fields.Why it matters: Connects computer vision to tightly targeted physical action.

fields.Price / access: unknown; contact supplier; medical use requires appropriate supervision.
fields.Key specs: Robotic hand exoskeleton, CE-marked medical device under EU MDR according to the manufacturer.
fields.Why it matters: Assistive actuation and user interaction with a clear clinical/research boundary.

fields.Price / access: unknown; research product, contact supplier.
fields.Key specs: Research-only hand exoskeletons with one to five active fingers, sensors such as position/force/EMG and control/telemetry APIs; non-certified devices.
fields.Why it matters: API-based sensing and control provide a concrete software entry point.

fields.Price / access: unknown; specialist fitting/training required.
fields.Key specs: Personal lower-limb exoskeleton supporting standing/walking for people with spinal cord injuries; current site emphasizes lightweight design and ease of use.
fields.Why it matters: Demonstrates user-centered assistive robotics and safety constraints.

fields.Price / access: unknown; professional inspection platform.
fields.Key specs: Underwater inspection robot with six degrees of freedom, optional wireless flyout and visual/NDT data collection; controlled through NAVIA interface.
fields.Why it matters: Submerged inspection adds communication, sensing and environmental constraints.

fields.Price / access: unknown; commercial vehicle integration.
fields.Key specs: Autonomous Navigation Technology supplies natural-feature navigation and integration for AGVs, AMRs and automated forklifts.
fields.Why it matters: A specialized navigation stack illustrates productization of mobile autonomy.

fields.Price / access: unknown; research prototype.
fields.Key specs: Polygon-based shape-changing modular research robot, listed by the lab as a space-travel-oriented reconfigurable robotics project.
fields.Why it matters: Mechanism reconfiguration provides a different path to versatility from a fixed humanoid body.

fields.Price / access: unknown; research prototype.
fields.Key specs: Origami-inspired untethered research robot listed among the laboratory's modular/soft robotics activities.
fields.Why it matters: Useful example of fabrication and actuation co-design.

fields.Price / access: unknown; research prototype.
fields.Key specs: Salamander-like research robot used to study locomotion and biological control.
fields.Why it matters: A physical testbed for neuroscience-inspired locomotion, not just learned policies.

fields.Price / access: unknown; research platform.
fields.Key specs: Salamander-inspired amphibious robot project used to investigate locomotion control with central pattern generators.
fields.Why it matters: Connects oscillatory control, body mechanics and amphibious locomotion.

fields.Price / access: unknown; research platform.
fields.Key specs: Snake/eel-inspired amphibious robot project for studying bio-inspired locomotion and central pattern generator controllers.
fields.Why it matters: Shows control/fabrication lessons beyond arms and wheeled bases.

fields.Price / access: unknown; contact supplier.
fields.Key specs: Piezoelectric six-axis force/torque sensor measuring Fx, Fy, Fz, Mx, My, Mz; a measurement component rather than a robot or simulator.
fields.Why it matters: Useful for teaching physical interaction measurement; low-cost access is not established.

fields.Price / access: unknown; proprietary industrial installation service.
fields.Key specs: Robotic Installation System for Elevators uses a modified industrial robot to drill holes and set anchors inside elevator shafts; source is a 2021 deployment description.
fields.Why it matters: Clear narrow-task automation case study with real safety and accuracy requirements.

fields.Price / access: unknown; commercial educational robot with open-source resources.
fields.Key specs: Open-source educational robot family developed with EPFL/ECAL and produced by Mobsya; current site announces Thymio 3 availability from September 2026.
fields.Why it matters: Simple embodied sensing/programming can support beginner onboarding and public workshops.

fields.Price / access: unknown; BFH advertises robot-park leasing for SMEs, student access requires agreement.
fields.Key specs: Collaborative arm listed as F&P P-Rob in BFH HuCE's robot park.
fields.Why it matters: A concrete collaborative-manipulation platform used in applied Swiss research.

fields.Price / access: unknown; confirm current educational/commercial licensing.
fields.Key specs: Robot/mechatronic simulation environment with distributed control through Python/Lua embedded scripts, C/C++ plugins and remote APIs; educational/commercial license conditions need checking.
fields.Why it matters: Software-first experimentation can isolate control and integration issues before physical deployment.

fields.Builder (if not in map): Japanese hardware supplier (official page spells 'Rokoro'; identity to verify); NTU Singapore
fields.Price / access: unknown; research system.
fields.Key specs: Social humanoid for interaction research; the official page credits Japanese hardware (supplier spelled 'Rokoro', identity needs checking), with software/platform and articulated hands developed at NTU Singapore and later Geneva. Not wholly Swiss-built; no clinical efficacy claim.
fields.Why it matters: A concrete platform illustrating embodied sensing/control constraints; not an immediate low-cost student procurement recommendation.

fields.Price / access: unknown; commercial/professional aviation system.
fields.Key specs: Hybrid-electric tilt-wing cargo drone; manufacturer advertises 20 kg useful load over 200 km, vertical takeoff/landing and in-house flight computer. These are vendor specifications, not independent performance tests.
fields.Why it matters: A concrete platform illustrating embodied sensing/control constraints; not an immediate low-cost student procurement recommendation.

fields.Price / access: unknown; commercial software.
fields.Key specs: Software operating layer for automated aerial logistics and remote fleet supervision from centralized control centers, described as transferable across airframes.
fields.Why it matters: Software-first experimentation can isolate control and integration issues before physical deployment.

fields.Price / access: unknown; professional ophthalmology platform, not student or clinical-use access.
fields.Key specs: Multi-ocular robotic station combining multiple optical measurement modalities, AI-assisted reporting and clinician-facing review. N/A form factor denotes a stationary medical measurement system, not an arm or mobile robot. Clinical efficacy and diagnostic accuracy are not independently validated here.
fields.Why it matters: Illustrates integrated sensing, motion and workflow automation in medicine; an educational case study, not a proposed student clinical project.

fields.Price / access: Research platform, not for sale
fields.Key specs: Series of KIT humanoids with KIT hands, used for grasping, bimanual manipulation and learning from human observation; individual specs unknown here.
fields.Why it matters: Germany's best-known academic humanoid line; shows a full research humanoid stack (ArmarX) end to end.

fields.Price / access: Open source (H2T GitLab)
fields.Key specs: Robot software framework and control architecture used on the ARMAR humanoids, alongside the Simox simulation/planning toolbox.
fields.Why it matters: Open framework students can study to see how a humanoid's software is organised.

fields.Price / access: Research platform
fields.Key specs: Humanoid upper body on a mobile base used as a platform for learning-based dexterous manipulation.
fields.Why it matters: Reference platform for AI dexterous manipulation in Europe.

fields.Price / access: Research platform
fields.Key specs: Wheeled humanoid for household and space-assistance research (teleoperation from orbit studies).
fields.Why it matters: Classic example of a wheeled humanoid for assistance tasks.

fields.Price / access: Research platform
fields.Key specs: Robust humanoid with variable-stiffness actuation and skilful manipulation.
fields.Why it matters: Shows how compliant actuators make humanoids robust to impacts.

fields.Price / access: Research platform
fields.Key specs: Torque-controlled humanoid used for learning-based control research.
fields.Why it matters: Torque control plus robot learning, the kind of research our lab wants to follow.

fields.Price / access: Research platform / collaborations
fields.Key specs: Two-wheeled, dynamically balancing (inverted pendulum) modular transport robot for load carriers and human-robot collaboration; fewer actuators than a humanoid.
fields.Why it matters: Cheap-to-build alternative to humanoids for logistics; balancing control is a nice student topic.

fields.Price / access: Commercial
fields.Key specs: Autonomous mobile picking robot that picks small boxes (originally shoe boxes) from shelves; now also spare parts and e-commerce items.
fields.Why it matters: One of the first perception-driven mobile picking robots in production.

fields.Price / access: Commercial
fields.Key specs: Autonomous KLT (small load carrier) robot / tugger for line feeding in production.
fields.Why it matters: Real-world intralogistics automation example.

fields.Price / access: Commercial; price unknown
fields.Key specs: 3D stereo sensor with on-board edge processing running the rc_reason software (bin picking, CAD matching, SLAM).
fields.Why it matters: Industrial 3D vision sensor for grasping projects.

fields.Price / access: Open source (GitHub, archived repo)
fields.Key specs: Kid-size soccer humanoid of the Hamburg Bit-Bots with public software repository.
fields.Why it matters: Open student-built humanoid; shows what a student team can build.

fields.Price / access: Research platform
fields.Key specs: Adult-size soccer humanoid with 3D-printed gears and new-generation actuators; won RoboCup 2023 AdultSize (66:0 goals).
fields.Why it matters: Proof that 3D-printed humanoids can win world championships.

fields.Price / access: Research platform
fields.Key specs: Musculoskeletal humanoid using muscles and tendons, developed for the ANA Avatar XPRIZE era.
fields.Why it matters: Student-built bio-inspired humanoid; strong outreach story.

fields.Price / access: Commercial turnkey cell
fields.Key specs: Modular turnkey automation cell for SMEs, configured through Unchained's online configurator.
fields.Why it matters: Example of packaging cobots for small manufacturers.

fields.Price / access: Commercial
fields.Key specs: Fourth-generation autonomy/teleoperation retrofit kit for yard and terminal trucks, aimed at series production (2024).
fields.Why it matters: Human-assisted autonomy for heavy vehicles in real deployment.

fields.Price / access: Commercial
fields.Key specs: Software layer of ARX Robotics' unmanned ground systems (alongside Gereon UGV and Hector).
fields.Why it matters: Shows the robot-OS layer strategy of a German field-robotics startup.

fields.Price / access: Commercial from 2026
fields.Key specs: Tractor-assisted robot that classifies crops vs weeds with AI and burns weeds by laser at 2-5 km/h; near 100% recognition claimed.
fields.Why it matters: Concrete vision-plus-actuation agri robot.

fields.Price / access: Research paper (2026); code availability unknown
fields.Key specs: Policy for humanoid loco-manipulation that predicts touch and force outcomes; trained with RL and VR teleoperation data, fusing tactile, multi-view vision and proprioception.
fields.Why it matters: Recent German industrial lab result on tactile robot learning.

fields.Price / access: Commercial (B2B for machine makers)
fields.Key specs: Autonomy OS with hybrid localization (with or without GNSS/RTK), field coverage planner and browser mission control.
fields.Why it matters: Agri autonomy software sold to OEMs.

fields.What they build: Maker of the cheapest widely sold legged robots: Go2 robot dog (from $1,600), R1 humanoid (from $4,900), G1 humanoid (from $13.5K), H1/H2 full-size humanoids, B2/A2 industrial quadrupeds, dexterous hands and LiDARs. Listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in Aug 2026 (IPO priced at ~61bn yuan / ~$9bn valuation).

Humanoid and service-robot company: Walker S2 industrial humanoid with autonomous hot-swappable battery, in mass production since Nov 2025 with orders reported above 800m yuan; also education and consumer robots. Signed a cooperation deal with Airbus in Jan 2026.

Founded 2023; world's largest humanoid shipper in H1 2026 per industry data cited by Global Times. Builds humanoids (A-series, X-series) and open-sources robot-learning assets: the AgiBot World dataset and the GO-1 foundation model. Began Hong Kong IPO process in Jul 2026; Oct 2026 round reported at ~RMB 50bn valuation.

Wheeled humanoid robots (G1, S1, ET1) driven by its own embodied foundation models (AstraBrain series). Raised ~$362M in early 2026 (investors incl. National AI Industry Investment Fund, Sinopec), described as China's highest-valued unlisted humanoid firm.

Started in rehabilitation robotics and now builds GR-series humanoids; ranked 6th globally in 2025 humanoid shipments (Omdia). In 2026 built Meta's 'Max' humanoid in ~3 months. Investors include SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Prosperity7.
EV maker XPeng's robotics unit; its IRON general-purpose humanoid rolled off a dedicated production line in Sep 2026 (core process automation >80%).

Collaborative robot arms (CR/CRA/Nova series), education desktop arms (Magician, Magician E6, MG400), the X-Trainer teleoperation platform for AI data collection, and ATOM full-size industrial humanoid (third batch launched Feb 2026, mass delivery targeted for 2026).

Mobile robot bases (SCOUT, RANGER, BUNKER, HUNTER, LIMO) and low-cost arms for physical-AI research: PiPER 6-DoF arm (4.2 kg, 1.5 kg payload, ±0.1 mm, ~$2,499), NERO, Cobot Magic / Mobile ALOHA kits, Pika data-collection kit. Open SDKs on GitHub.
Quadruped robots (Jueying Lite3, X30, LYNX M20 wheel-legged), DR02 all-weather humanoid and J-series joint modules; filed for a 2.5bn-yuan STAR Market IPO in May 2026.

Wheeled dual-arm R1 robots (from $39,999), LEMO A1Z 6-DoF arm (from $2,999) and LEMO desktop dual-arm platform, plus open-source VLA models (G0, G0.5) in the GalaxeaVLA repo. Raised a 1bn-yuan Series B in Feb 2026 (10bn-yuan valuation).
Tsinghua University spinout building STAR1 and L7 humanoids and dexterous hands; raised ~500m yuan Series A in Jul 2025.
KUAVO humanoid series (KUAVO 4Pro, KUAVO 5) sold as research/education and service platforms; filed for a ChiNext IPO in May 2026 (2.6bn-yuan target).

nodes.name: Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics (X-Humanoid)

fields.What they build: State-backed humanoid innovation center: Tiangong humanoids (TianGong 3.0 in mass delivery H2 2026), embodied-AI software, and the open RoboMIND dataset (300k+ dual-arm trajectories, 700+ tasks; 20m downloads by Sep 2026).
Non-profit AI institute; releases open embodied-AI 'brain' models such as RoboBrain 2.0 (7B checkpoint on Hugging Face, Jun 2025) and later RoboBrain 2.5, trained with its FlagScale framework.
Major state AI lab whose InternRobotics group open-sources InternVLA-M1 (spatially guided VLA, MIT license) and the InternUtopia (ex-GRUtopia) embodied-AI simulation platform.
Warehouse robotics: shelf/tote/pallet AMRs, sorting robots, picking robot arm and fleet software; listed in Hong Kong in Jul 2025.
Leading domestic industrial-robot and servo maker (called 'first share of industrial robots'); in Sep 2026 consolidated a humanoid robot business by acquiring Estun Kuozhuo.
Annual Beijing robotics expo and conference; 2026 edition (19-23 Aug) showed 3,000+ products. Shares the season with the World Humanoid Robot Games (2nd edition Aug 2026).
Shanghai's annual AI conference; 2026 edition (17-20 Jul) had 1,100+ exhibitors and 3,000+ products, with humanoid robots and VLA/world models as a central theme.
Top Chinese university for robotics/embodied AI; source of spinouts such as RobotEra; its Youth2Real team won two tracks at ICRA 2026 manipulation competitions.

German motion-technology supplier of bearings and drives, including actuators (motor, gearbox and sensing combined into a robot joint). In August 2026 it announced formed strain wave gearboxes for humanoid joints, with mass production planned for 2027. Its May 2026 agreement with UK robot maker Humanoid targets a four-digit number of robots deployed by 2032 and a seven-digit actuator supply commitment; these are staged future commitments, not completed deliveries.

Swiss maker of precision DC and brushless motors, gearheads, encoders and motor controllers. At Automate 2026 it demonstrated an IP67 integrated drive and humanoid joint actuators combining motors, gearboxes, encoders and control electronics. Its Young Engineers Program offers selected student teams subsidized prices or product sponsorship; eligibility is not guaranteed.
fields.Warm contact path: unknown; public application route: maxon Young Engineers Program (not a warm introduction)

fields.What they build: German maker of strain wave gears and precision drive systems for robotics, medical equipment, aerospace and space. A strain wave gear uses an elastically deforming gear element to obtain high reduction ratios in a compact joint; the company markets zero-backlash gear products. No market-share claim is established here.
German family company for grippers, toolholding and workholding. In 2026 it signed a partnership with Bosch Robotics to co-design an industrial-grade robot hand for humanoid robots.

German family-owned automation supplier headquartered in Esslingen am Neckar. It provides pneumatic and electric drive technologies, automation software and AI solutions, while Festo Didactic supplies technical education and training systems.

German motion-plastics supplier of self-lubricating bearings, cable chains and automation components. Its ReBeL cobot arms form part of Iggy Rob, a wheeled mobile manipulator announced in 2025 with two arms, bionic hands, lidar and 3D cameras. The 2025 coverage cited an intended price of €47,999 (about $54,500 then), not a verified current quote. In June 2026 igus announced the Iggy Rob Home service variant from €55,000; that is a different variant and price from the 2025 industrial announcement.
Danish maker of end-of-arm tooling for cobots: electric and vacuum grippers, force/torque sensors, tool changers, plus D:PLOY software for palletizing, CNC tending and packaging.

German chipmaker supplying power semiconductors, microcontrollers, sensors, connectivity and safety/security components for robots. Its Infineon Mobile Robot (IMR) demonstrates these subsystems. AdapTronics won its 2026 humanoid robotics startup challenge; Reuters reported a March 2026 Nvidia partnership covering robot hardware and digital-twin development.

Franco-Italian chipmaker headquartered in Geneva, supplying STM32 microcontrollers, MEMS motion sensors and motor-control electronics. In 2026 it acquired a stake in RoBee builder Oversonic Robotics. Reuters reported its March 2026 Nvidia partnership focused on connecting camera and motion sensors to Nvidia-based robot systems; this is not evidence that ST builds RoBee.

Dutch chipmaker: processors, sensing (radar, vision, UWB), Ethernet/TSN and CAN networking, security and functional safety for drones, AMRs and humanoids. Announced physical-AI work with Nvidia in Mar 2026.

Dutch edge-AI chip startup. Its Metis chip (~214 TOPS at ~10 W) uses digital in-memory computing to run vision models on robots and cameras. Raised more than $250M in Feb 2026 (led by Innovation Industries, with BlackRock and Samsung Catalyst).

Italian electronics and software platform, now a Qualcomm subsidiary, known for open-source microcontroller boards and the Arduino development environment. Its 2026 VENTUNO Q pairs a Qualcomm Dragonwing IQ8 processor (up to 40 dense TOPS of AI compute) with an STM32H5 microcontroller for real-time control. Arduino boards were already used in robots before this dedicated robotics product.
UK maker of low-cost Arm single-board computers (Raspberry Pi 5), Pico microcontroller boards (RP2 chips), cameras and add-on boards; widely used as the 'brain' of hobby and student robots.
German industrial sensor maker: safety laser scanners, lidar, 2D/3D vision and other sensors used on AMRs and in factory automation.

UK maker of the Shadow Dexterous Hand (tendon-driven, five-fingered research hand with tactile fingertips) and the DEX-EE hand. In Oct 2026 it started a six-month project with Fraunhofer IFF on dexterous hands, tactile sensing and teleoperation for manufacturing.
Swiss ETH spin-off making compact 6-axis force-torque sensors (MiniONE, Rokubi, SensONE, LaxONE) with integrated electronics and IMU, plus tactile sensors, so robots can 'feel' contact forces.

German provider of integrated servo drives, motion-control electronics and functional safety for robotics. In August 2026 it announced a partnership with Stabilus to develop and manufacture integrated humanoid joint actuators. The partners target scalable production; the announcement does not establish that the joint product line is already shipping.

Zurich physical-AI startup, legally Eta Robotics AG, developing force-aware dexterous manipulation. Rather than relying only on vision or fingertip sensors, it captures force information through actuators and redesigns the hardware-to-model stack. It emerged from stealth in October 2026 with a reported $30M pre-seed round from redalpine, Notion Capital, firstminute and angels including Arthur Mensch and Yann LeCun.

Budapest startup developing 3D Tissue Braiding to manufacture compliant robot bodies. It produces a scaffold, braids soft tissues and routes tendons, then connects actuators: this is not a claim that motors emerge fully assembled from the braiding step. Its investor confirmed a $7.2M pre-seed in February 2026, including individual angels from OpenAI and Hugging Face, not corporate investment by those companies.

Italian startup developing electro-adhesive gripping interfaces with tactile feedback. Its proprietary thin-film Electro Active Adhesive Layer (EAAL) is mounted on a conformable backing and activated by a 24 V electronic unit to hold objects without suction or fingers. It won Infineon’s 2026 humanoid robotics Startup Challenge; suitability for a specific object still needs testing.

German carmaker and Europe's most visible buyer of humanoid robots. After using Figure AI humanoids (Figure 02, then Figure 03 since June 2026) in its US plant Spartanburg, it started Europe's first humanoid pilot in a car plant at Leipzig in 2026 with Hexagon Robotics' wheeled AEON humanoid, delivering parts to the line in battery and component production. Runs a new competence centre for AI + robotics integration.

German carmaker testing Apptronik's Apollo humanoid robots for intralogistics (moving parts and modules to assembly workers) at the Mercedes-Benz Digital Factory Campus in Berlin-Marienfelde. Workers teach the robots by teleoperation and augmented reality (a human remotely drives the robot to record demonstrations). Mercedes also invested in Apptronik.

Europe's largest online fashion retailer and a major buyer of AI picking robots. Installing up to 50 Nomagic 'Richard' item-picking robots in its European fulfilment centres (2026) and using Sereact dual-arm robots to sort returns at Ceva Logistics sites in Germany and Poland; also invested in Sereact's Series B.

German logistics group. Its contract-logistics arm DHL Supply Chain has deployed more than 8,000 robotic systems worldwide (picking, packing, put-away) since its first robotics bet in 2017, and uses SVT Robotics' SOFTBOT platform as one integration layer to plug many robot vendors into its warehouse software.

UK online-grocery tech company that designs and installs fully robotic warehouses for retailers worldwide: a grid where swarms of 'bots' (more than 17,000 in its sites) fetch storage boxes, plus robotic picking arms. In July 2026 it won a deal to build a robotic warehouse for an unnamed European retailer (site due to go live in its 2028 financial year).

German automation giant: makes the PLCs, digital-twin and fleet software that factories use to plug robots in (Siemens Xcelerator), and is itself a test customer. In 2025-26 it ran a proof of concept with UK startup Humanoid's wheeled HMND 01 robot moving totes to a conveyor at its Erlangen electronics factory (60 tote moves/hour, 8h+ uptime).

European aircraft maker with big French operations (Toulouse). Created an in-house 'Airbus Robotics' unit in 2023 that builds its own shop-floor robots (e.g. the 4 kg CabinMarker for seat-track installation, FlexTrack drilling robot, exoskeletons) and bought UBTech's Walker S2 humanoid in 2026 for aviation-manufacturing trials.

Italian robotics system integrator (formerly Stellantis' captive supplier, now independent) that designs turnkey automated production lines, EV battery lines and also sells its own robots and cobots. In Oct 2026 it partnered with NVIDIA to run Isaac Sim digital twins and Jetson AI compute inside its robot controllers; after leaving Stellantis it is expanding into battery recycling/storage and warehouse logistics.

Austrian warehouse-automation integrator: shuttles, bots, pocket sorters, AMRs and AI picking robots plus warehouse software. Its AI-vision Pick-it-Easy Robot (~450 picks/hour) was added in 2026 to Edeka's fresh-meat centre in Germany; it opened a Robotics & AI Innovation Hub near Boston (KNAPPRobotics.ai).

German family-owned intralogistics group: storage, conveying, picking systems and warehouse software. In April 2026 it integrated its fully automatic 'SSI Piece Picking' robot into Würth Industrie Service's logistics centre in Bad Mergentheim; won several 2026 materialfluss product awards.

Austrian warehouse-automation integrator (50+ years) building shuttle systems (FlashPick) and the RovoFlex AI picking robot with camera system and PickCenter software; customer references include Dinosol and Kärcher.

Swiss warehouse-automation integrator (part of KUKA): pallet high-bay warehouses, AutoStore cube storage, robotic case and item picking (ItemPiQ robot, up to 1,000 items/hour) and healthcare/hospital automation. Delivered the AutoStore system that Cognibotics' picking cell works with at Nowaste Logistics (Sweden).
Dutch integrator of logistics automation for airports (baggage handling, robotic loading) and parcel/warehouse sites; since April 2026 part of Toyota Automated Logistics (Toyota Industries).

German builder of car paint shops and final-assembly lines; has sold 20,000+ painting robots. Its 4th-generation EcoRP4 paint robot entered production in 2026 (20,000th robot delivered to Ford Valencia).

German tech group whose supply-chain business sells warehouse software and automation. In Oct 2026 it took a stake in NAiSE, a German maker of vendor-agnostic fleet-management software that lets AGVs/AMRs (autonomous mobile robots) from different brands and manual forklifts share one control layer.

Belgian startup founded in 2026 offering 'Humanoids-as-a-Service': factories pay a monthly fee and Motion handles robot selection, task training, data collection, IT integration, fleet management, financing and maintenance. Raised a $2M pre-seed led by Extantia (Aug 2026); five paid pilots in Belgian factories (loading crates, packing, conveyor placement).

French group that is Unitree's master distributor in Europe and acts as integrator: use-case assessment, robot selection, systems integration, functional safety, deployment and training. Runs one of Europe's first humanoid pilots in live car-parts manufacturing with Novares (2026), using Unitree humanoids.

Fraunhofer Institute for Manufacturing Engineering and Automation: applied research that brings robots into factories. In 2026 it launched an independent benchmark that tests humanoid robots (e.g. Unitree G1) on six industry criteria (energy efficiency, cleanroom fit, data security...), runs ROS 2-Industrial trainings, and is part of the euROBIN network.

Munich trade fair (Messe München) for robotics and automation, presented as the world's largest robotics portfolio across the value chain, focusing on Physical AI. Hosts munich_i with TUM's MIRMI institute (Hightech Summit, AI.Society show, Robothon developer challenge); publishes the automatica Trend Index survey (2026: 82% of German decision-makers want more humanoid subsidies).

lesson.summary: Hugging Face's LeRobot team builds open-source tools, datasets, and policies for learning from real robot demonstrations.
lesson.lesson_md:
## In one sentence
Hugging Face's LeRobot team builds open-source tools, datasets, and policies for learning from real robot demonstrations.

## What they do in robotics
LeRobot links robot hardware with dataset recording, model training, and policy evaluation. Its docs cover SO-101 setup, real-world imitation learning, SmolVLA, and commands such as `lerobot-record` and `lerobot-train`. Hugging Face hosts code, model checkpoints, and datasets so a team can inspect and share an experiment rather than passing opaque files between laptops.

## Why they matter for 42AI
The stack is a practical starting point for a student lab with software experience and limited mechanical background. A SO-101 team can teleoperate a task, label demonstrations, train a baseline, and compare results on held-out trials. The tools lower integration effort, but students still need to understand motor calibration, camera synchronization, data licenses, and the difference between a pretrained model and a validated robot behavior.

## How to engage
Start with the current LeRobot docs and repository issue tracker; reproduce a small supported workflow before filing a question. When sharing a bug, include the robot type, package version, command, logs, dataset configuration, and a minimal way to reproduce it. A useful contribution might improve a driver, add a dataset validation check, or document a clear setup failure. A demo video or benchmark should include the task, trial count, and failure cases, not just the best run.

lesson.summary: ETH Zurich's Robotic Systems Lab develops legged and mobile robots and studies how they operate in complex real-world environments.
lesson.lesson_md:
## In one sentence
ETH Zurich's Robotic Systems Lab develops legged and mobile robots and studies how they operate in complex real-world environments.

## What they do in robotics
The RSL builds platforms such as ANYmal, a quadruped designed to inspect and traverse difficult terrain, and conducts research in locomotion, perception, and autonomy. Its public lab and robot pages show how algorithms are evaluated on physical machines rather than only on benchmark plots. The group also publishes open software, including tools used for legged-robot learning.

## Why they matter for 42AI
RSL is a useful reference for comparing a low-cost tabletop arm with a robot that must maintain balance and footholds outdoors. A learned gait has to tolerate uneven ground, sensor noise, actuator limits, and repeated impacts. The lab's papers, robot footage, and code let students inspect a research path from model to hardware and identify which lessons generalize to smaller projects.

## How to engage
Read a recent paper and watch the associated robot demonstration before contacting a researcher. Ask one specific question about an open-source tool, experiment setup, student event, or reproducibility detail. If reproducing a result, state the robot and software version, simulator settings, dataset, and measured outcomes. RSL's public materials are research references; they do not imply that a particular robot or lab resource is available to outside teams.

lesson.lesson_md:
## In one sentence
Pollen Robotics is a French robotics company known for open-source humanoid and expressive robots, now connected to Hugging Face's robotics work.

## What they do in robotics
Pollen develops robots including Reachy, a humanoid platform, and Reachy Mini, a smaller expressive desktop robot. The company emphasizes accessible hardware and software that developers can use to experiment with interaction and embodied AI. Hugging Face announced its acquisition of Pollen Robotics and described plans to bring open-source robots into a broader machine-learning community.

## Why they matter for 42AI
Pollen offers a concrete example of how an open robot platform can connect research, product engineering, and developer tooling. Reachy Mini demonstrates that human-robot interaction is not only navigation or grasping: head motion, gaze, and expressive behavior are part of the interface. Students can compare such a platform with SO-101, which is optimized for low-cost arm manipulation and learning rather than expressive interaction.

## How to engage
Read the current product and developer documentation before proposing a project. Identify whether an idea needs a robot, simulation, or only a dataset; include a clear task, expected contribution, and available student time. Track official Pollen and Hugging Face announcements for software and hardware availability, since acquisition and product details can change. The open-source repository and model organization are better starting points than a generic partnership request.

Industrial arms, collaborative CRX robots, CNC automation and ROBOGUIDE robot simulation. The current product page includes 2024-2026 controller and physical-AI updates.
fields.Warm contact path: FANUC France contact page lists Lisses, Marnaz, Rennes and Les Echets; approach the Lisses team or FANUC Academy through the public form. No personal introduction known.

fields.What they build: MOTOMAN industrial robots, HC collaborative arms, servo motors and automation systems. Cobots support hand-guided teaching; this is not the same as learned imitation policies.
fields.Warm contact path: Yaskawa Europe public robotics contact and local-contact finder; the global site also lists France. No personal introduction known.

fields.What they build: aibo companion robots combine sensing, expressive motion and cloud-supported behavior. A developer program is linked from the live aibo site; this does not make the robot open hardware.
Honda Robotics researches avatar robots and UNI-ONE mobility assistance. Its official strategy explicitly moves beyond a single general-purpose ASIMO-style humanoid toward task-specific assistance.

Japan-based Toyota develops the Human Support Robot (HSR), a mobile arm for domestic assistance. The cited 2015 developer-community program is historical, not evidence that a French student lab can borrow an HSR today. Toyota Research Institute in the US is not this row.

Develops AI chips, computing infrastructure and AI applications, with industrial-robot partners among its shareholders. Spun out Preferred Robotics; the latter now builds Kachaka products. PFR reports joint development of PLaMo-SemGround for indoor mobile-robot scene understanding in September 2026, not a verified public model release.

PFN spin-off building small autonomous mobile robots: Kachaka Pro, Kachaka Evo and the HAPiiBOT floor-cleaning robot co-developed with Amano. Publishes a Kachaka Python/ROS 2 API SDK; hardware and the full autonomy stack are not thereby open-source.
fields.Warm contact path: unknown; the official Kachaka API GitHub Discussions is a public technical route, not a warm introduction.

fields.What they build: Builds teachless robot controllers and MujinOS, combining perception, motion planning and no-code orchestration for factories and warehouses. Japan-founded business, distinct from the US subsidiary whose website supplies the cited corporate history. Its opened official news index documents a Series C in September 2023 and a $233M raise in December 2025; the Japan site independently confirms manufacturing/logistics deployments.
fields.Warm contact path: Corporate history verifies Mujin Europe opened in Eindhoven in October 2023; approach through the official company contact, not a known personal introduction.

fields.What they build: Develops AI-driven and remotely operated manipulation systems. Its September 2025 announcement documents TX Ghost beverage-restocking pilots at select Tokyo 7-Eleven stores; its 2026 site discusses humanoids and robot foundation-model development.

Develops collaborative picking AMRs, automated storage/retrieval systems and multi-robot control. Its live site includes customer warehouse case studies and 2024-2026 product news; performance claims are vendor claims, not independent comparisons.

Kawada group company building NEXTAGE dual-arm industrial humanoids, including NXA and Fillie, plus OPEN research variants with extensible software. Also lists HRP-2/3/4 research platforms. A humanoid upper body does not imply bipedal walking.

Japan national research institute; its humanoid group developed HRP-5P for heavy manipulation such as gypsum-board installation. The 2018 prototype is a historical research platform, not evidence of a current commercial offering.

University robotics laboratory researching integrated perception/action, assistive humanoids, musculoskeletal robots such as Kengoro and aerial robots. Its research index also lists open-source robot software. Classified as School to represent the university/laboratory entry together, not as a second duplicate university row.

Biennial robot exhibition at Tokyo Big Sight spanning production robots, service robots and components. The live site reports the 2025 show and says the next iREX is scheduled for early December 2027; RoboNext 2026 is a separate event.
Industry association publishing Japanese robot statistics and membership information, and linking to robot exhibitions. Its English site has quarterly statistics through July-September 2026.

Volunteer ROS community organizing developer meetings, study sessions, workshops and hackathons. Its official GitHub profile links connpass, Slack and organizer contact details; it is not the builder of ROS itself.
fields.Warm contact path: unknown; official GitHub profile links community Slack, connpass and the public organizer email. These are cold outreach channels.

fields.What they build: Investment holding group with documented participation in Telexistence's 2023 Series B. The same announcement distinguishes SoftBank Group as investor from SoftBank Robotics Group as a strategic business partner; no Pepper/NAO builder attribution is inferred.

Self-balancing exoskeletons (Atalante X used at 150+ clinical and research sites; Eve personal exoskeleton) and, since 2025, the Calvin-40 industrial humanoid developed with Renault. Opened a robot production site in Paris.

Mirokaï social robots (Miroki and Miroka): manga-style robots with a head and two arms riding on a motorised ball, deployed in hospitals, nursing homes, hotels and Lyon airport. Founded 2021 by ex-Aldebaran Jérôme Monceaux; Google DeepMind Gemini trusted tester.

Lightweight, low-cost general-purpose humanoid robots (Northstar design, Version 0 prototype, designed and assembled in Paris). Co-founded by Rémi Cadène, ex-Tesla Optimus and former lead of Hugging Face LeRobot.
fields.Warm contact path: Via the Hugging Face LeRobot team (Cadène's former team)

fields.What they build: French LLM company that entered robotics in July 2026 with Robostral Navigate, an 8B single-camera navigation model trained on simulated data with RL; organised a Physical AI & Robotics hackathon in Paris (April 2025) with Hugging Face LeRobot.
Synthetic data platform for physical AI: describe a 3D scene, vary it millions of ways and get perfect ground truth for training robot/vision models. Raised $10M seed (Inovia) in Nov 2026.
Autonomous robots for existing (brownfield) warehouses: picking, sorting, palletizing, container unloading, packing. Founded 2025; Station F Future 40 2025.
Modular warehouse robotics: TAK-ONE system that slides parcels and bins horizontally and vertically across levels (compact buffer/sorting). €10M round in 2025 (Supernova Invest, Bpifrance).
3D LiDAR SLAM software (Exwayz Engine): mapping, centimetre localization and perception for robots and autonomous vehicles, CPU-only. CentraleSupélec 21st accelerator; €1M raised.
Microrobots the size of a grain of rice that travel inside the brain for minimally invasive neurosurgery. Founded 2017 in Paris; based at AP-HP Hôtel-Dieu; $28M raised in 2025.
Maestro surgical-assistant robot for laparoscopy (holds and moves instruments for the surgeon); 2026 software update turned it into a 'physical AI' platform. Backed by Sofinnova and Cathay Health.
Marker-less robotic assistant for total knee arthroplasty (orthopaedic surgery), under development (not yet cleared).
Swan: robot that captures standardized full-body dermoscopic skin images for early skin-cancer detection. Raised $18M in 2026 (Sonder Capital, Deeptech 2030 Fund).

AI-piloted autonomous drones (interceptors, strike and reconnaissance), radar/EW payloads and command software. Founded 2024, French defence unicorn; $200M Series B led by Dassault Aviation (Jan 2026).
Modular autonomous underwater vehicles (low-cost subsea drone swarms) for fleet defence. Founded 2025; Y Combinator P26; Station F Future 40 2026.
Real-time low-latency (≈8 ms) infrastructure for robot teleoperation, monitoring, training-data collection and human takeover; founded by VLC lead developer Jean-Baptiste Kempf; open-source strategy.
Agentic 'common brain' / OS that orchestrates fleets of heterogeneous robots and devices through natural language.
Teaching infrastructure that trains existing robot models on customer-specific jobs they fail at (XR + 3D computer vision).
Collaborative robots for industrial sanding/finishing; CEA-List spin-off; €7M raised in Feb 2026.
Autonomous forklift robots (AGV/AMR hybrids with LiDAR navigation) built on OEM chassis; 2025 sales €31.4M.
Goods-to-person warehouse robots (mobile robots carrying shelves to pickers); founded 2013, HQ and R&D in Paris.
Outdoor logistics robots (autonomous car-parking/vehicle-moving robots); founded 2015, HQ Paris.
Continues NAO (and Aldebaran legacy) development after Maxvision bought Aldebaran's core assets in July 2025; social humanoids for research, education and healthcare.
Drones, now mainly professional/defence micro-UAVs such as ANAFI UKR (sovereign ISR micro-drone, 2025).
Event-based (neuromorphic) vision sensors and software: cameras that only report pixel changes, giving very low latency perception for robots and drones.
Infrastructure-based physical AI: 3D LiDAR software that tracks people/vehicle flows in airports, factories and cities.
Maritime robotics (drones/underwater vehicles) and inertial navigation systems; high-tech industrial group.
Car maker; strategic investor in Wandercraft and first customer for its Calvin-40 humanoid for factory tasks.
IT/engineering services group; tests Unitree robots with Orano for operations in radioactive zones.
Aircraft maker; led Harmattan AI's $200M Series B (Jan 2026) to back autonomous drones.
World's largest startup campus; hosts Genesis AI, Bleu Robotics, Marso, AICE (Future 40), MACHINA physical-AI summit and GOSIM robotics hackathon.
Sorbonne Université / CNRS robotics lab (Jussieu): learning robots, humanoids, haptics, medical and assistive robotics.
Inria's Paris centre; WILLOW (with ENS/PSL) works on computer vision, robot learning and manipulation; the Inria Paris Robotics Days showcase robotics research.
CEA technology institute for digital systems: cobotics, teleoperation, exoskeletons, simulation; spawned ISYBOT and others.
ENSTA Paris computer-science and systems lab working on autonomous mobile robots and human-robot interaction.
Mines Paris PSL robotics centre: autonomous vehicles, LiDAR perception, SLAM, virtual reality.
Tuition-free peer-learning coding school; home of 42AI. Hosted the LeRobot worldwide hackathon (June 2025).
University hosting ISIR and robotics master's programmes.
Engineering school with robotics curriculum and the U2IS lab.
Engineering school (Institut Polytechnique de Paris, Palaiseau); robotics research and student projects.
Engineering school; its 21st accelerator incubated Exwayz.
Engineering school hosting the CAOR robotics centre.
42 Paris's AI student association; launching the Robotics Lab; co-host of the 2025 LeRobot hackathon.
Robotics/AI builder community running hands-on robotics hackathons (e.g. Unaite x GOSIM at Station F, May 2026) and 'Paris Builds' events.
Global open-source robot-learning community around LeRobot, SO-100/SO-101 arms and shared datasets, steered from Paris.

Europe's largest tech show (June, Paris); 2026 featured humanoid parades and industrial robotics demos.
Physical-AI gathering at Station F (2026) asking whether Paris can be Europe's physical-AI capital.
France's main industry trade show with a large robotics universe (AGV/AMR, cobots, welding, painting).
World's largest defence & security show; 2026 edition full of UGVs and drones.
Physical AI & Robotics hackathon by Mistral AI with Hugging Face LeRobot (April 2025, Paris).
AI summit hackathon programme by Artefact in Paris.
French public investment bank; invests in robotics (Galam, Isybot via Amorçage Industriel funds, Deeptech plan).
Deeptech VC; led Galam Robotics' €10M round.
Life-science VC; investor in Moon Surgical.

Korean automotive group and Robotics LAB. Builds MobED, a modular wheeled robot that keeps its payload level on uneven ground, offered as Basic and autonomous Pro configurations.
